units: mm, minutes; model frame of cad/lpbf_low.py (origin at the floor's top centre, +y to the back)
how_to_animate: Start from CHAMBER_OPS[part]['blank']; in each setup turn the part by rotation_model_to_machine (rows are machine x, y, z in model coordinates; for the 4th-axis setup use index[A]), and for each op cut, in order, the solids it lists: 'FR-xx'/'FP-xx' are lpbf_low.CHAMBER_OPS[...]['ops'] entries, 'J:<key>' the tools in joints.CUTS['Process chamber body' / 'Chamber floor plate'] with that key. The spindle stays vertical (machine +z). FR-01 / FP-01 is the outside trim and both faces, shared between the two flat setups (bottom face and lower half of the profile first, then the rest).

mill.atc: 20 pockets, tool max Ø89 mm / 5.4 kg, tool-to-tool 4.2 s

endmill_6061.doc: regular LOC: heavy roughing ADOC <= 1.5 D, RDOC 30-50 %; light roughing ADOC = LOC, RDOC 15-25 %; longer than regular LOC: light roughing ADOC <= 2 D, RDOC 10-15 %; finishing RDOC 3-5 %
endmill_6061.source: Helical aluminium parameters (HAL-C-3 / H35AL-3 / H40ALV-3 / HAL-3), https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0612/0733/files/Helical_Aluminum_Parameters.pdf (22:32 UTC)

hem.note: Helical HEM: RDOC 7-30 % D, ADOC up to 2 D; 1/2 in. 3-flute in 6061 at 18,000 rpm, 500 ipm, 40 % x 2 D = 100 in3/min

long_reach.note: Haas: 'Reduce cut depth and feed by 50% for long-flute or long-reach tools'; Helical: finishing deeper than 3 x D 'may require a 50% feed rate reduction', and use necked tools beyond 2-3 x D
long_reach.source: Haas HM42-3FL chart (22:41 UTC); Helical guidebook pp. 7, 10, 11

facemill.source: Haas HPAL2 insert chart, wrought aluminium (22:41 UTC)

drill.source: Haas HCD TSC carbide drills, wrought aluminium (22:41 UTC)

tap.source: Haas metric aluminium taps 10-15 m/min; Haas ALU tap chart 50-65 SFM (22:41 UTC)

deflection.note: end mill as a solid rod of 0.7-0.8 x D in delta = F L^3 / (3 E I), I = pi D_e^4 / 64

waterjet.note: WARDJet: 4 in. aluminium at 0.72 ipm (Q5) to 4.2 ipm (Q1); speed ~ 1/thickness^1.15 gives 0.50-2.9 ipm at 5.5 in. (scaled)
waterjet.source: https://www.wardjet.com/nozzle-and-orifice/ (22:39 UTC); UF EML2322L waterjet notes (22:35 UTC)

setups.name: the four walls on the 4th axis (one clamping, four index angles)
setups.machine: VF-4 with an HRT210-class rotary (A axis along machine X)
setups.fixture: the same dummy-floor plate bolted to the HRT210 platter, the frame on it with its bottom against the plate (2 pins + 18 M4 screws), so the frame's z axis is the A axis. The frame swings 188.3 mm about it, more than the HRT210's 152.4 mm centre height: put the rotary on a 2-1/2 in. (63.5 mm) riser so A sits 215.9 mm above the table (27 mm clear). No tailstock: the open top overhangs ~150 mm, 4.3 kg + the plate, inside the 38.6 kg unsupported rating
setups.alternatives: A along the frame's x instead (it swings only 127 mm, so no riser), held by its side walls between a platter plate and the tailstock: one clamping for top, bottom, front and back, but the two side walls then need their own setups, and the big sealing faces are cut on the rotary rather than flat on the table. Same three setups; this plan keeps the faces that matter most on the table.
